title: 50M-Row User Schema Column Rename Zero-Downtime Migration
businessContext: A social and commerce platform has 50,000,000 records in the `users` table. The engineering team needs to rename and split `full_name` into `first_name` and `last_name`. Running `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN first_name ...; UPDATE users SET ...` in a single migration script locks the table exclusively for 25 minutes, taking the entire platform offline.
problemStatement: Design a multi-phase, zero-downtime database migration strategy (Expand and Contract / Parallel Run pattern). Describe the schema changes, dual-writing application layer, backfill script with throttling, and final deprecation cleanup without locking production tables.
constraints: Both old and new application versions must function concurrently during deployment.
Backfill must not starve database replication lag or max out IOPS.

systemDesignReqs.scale: 50 Million rows, 8,000 active writes/sec, PostgreSQL primary with 3 read replicas.
functional: Migrate full_name column into first_name and last_name columns.
Support dual-writing and zero-downtime cutover across application rolling restarts.
nonFunctional: Replication lag on read replicas must stay under 1 second.
Backward and forward API compatibility across deployment versions.
assumptions: PostgreSQL version 14+ running on AWS RDS / Aurora.

candidateTasks: Map out the 5 phases of the Expand and Contract (Parallel Run) migration pattern.
Show how to add nullable columns without rewriting the table or acquiring heavy AccessExclusiveLocks.
Design a background backfill script that batches updates in chunks of 1,000 with sleep intervals.
Explain when to drop the old column and remove dual-writing code.
hints: Phase 1: Expand (add new nullable columns). Phase 2: Dual-write in app or trigger. Phase 3: Backfill historical rows in batches. Phase 4: Read from new columns. Phase 5: Contract (drop old columns).
In PostgreSQL 11+, adding a column with a default value does NOT rewrite the table, but backfilling 50M rows in a single UPDATE will bloat WAL and hold locks.
alternativeApproaches: Using PostgreSQL database triggers for dual-writing during the transition instead of application code.
Using tools like `pg-online-schema-change` or GitHub's `gh-ost` for MySQL.
commonMistakes: Adding a NOT NULL constraint without a default during Phase 1 (causes immediate deployment failure for existing rows and old app versions).
Running backfills without sleeping or chunking, triggering replica lag alerts and disk fillups.
